title: Mexico Demands US Accountability for 17 Mexican Nationals Who Died in ICE Custody or Operations Since Trump Took Office
detail: CNN reported July 14, 2026 that at least 17 Mexican nationals have died in connection with the Trump administration's mass immigration crackdown since January 2025, according to the Mexican government. Fourteen died in the custody of immigration enforcement — in detention centers or medical facilities they had been sent to — while three, including Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, died during enforcement operations themselves. Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said the country shared the pain of the victims' families and announced Mexico would request U.S. criminal charges over the deaths, including Salgado Araujo's July 7 shooting. On July 14, Mexico began filing complaints with U.S. state and federal prosecutors requesting criminal investigations and sent cease-and-desist letters to private companies operating the U.S. detention centers where Mexican nationals had died. Families described harrowing conditions to CNN: inadequate medical care, prolonged confinement, and a lack of transparency from ICE about the circumstances of their relatives' deaths — concerns that echo the June 25 HRW/PHR 'Dying in Detention' report documenting a record U.S. detention mortality rate.
